newsitem.title: FINLAND: Helsinki off as Wall St jitters sideline investors.
newsitem.headline: Helsinki off as Wall St jitters sideline investors.

text.p: Shares on Monday echoed Wall Street's pre-weekend slide but brokers were undaunted, saying clues on the chances for the rally to resume were due this week.
The HEX index fell 1.06 percent to 2,707.2 with volume just over 500 million markka -- still heavy by last year's standards but thinner than of late.

U.S. fourth quarter employment cost data on Tuesday and U.S. GDP data due on Friday are expected to give a hint of the Federal Reserve's interest rate decision on its next open market committee meeting on February 4-5, brokers said.

Pohjola continued firm most of the session, reaching a new 1990s record at 149.00 markka after Goldman Sachs' reinstated a buy, but fell into negative ground to close off 2.50 markka at 139.00 after Moody's said it may cut the insurer's rating.
Trade in Pohjola was a lively 40 million markka.
Nokia fell below its New York close amid mild profit taking, ending 6.50 markka down at 310.00, but dealings were calm at less than a third of the bourse total.
Engineering group Santasalo ended at a new 48.00 markka life-high, up 1.10, on improved 1996 earnings and dividend.
"Santasalo is one of the small caps that has always been sort of promising, but is just now starting to fulfil expectations, " one broker said.
Food group Raisio extended last week's losses, down five markka at 404.00.
It was hit last week by a newspaper report of a patent application for a plant sterol powder which was dubbed a competitor to Raisio's Benecol margarine.
Nerves also mounted amid uncertainty ahead of the corporate result season starting next week with Cultor, KCI Konecranes, Finnlines and Kone, brokers said.
